shortDescription: The Czech economy expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter, driven mainly by household consumption and investments, the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Friday.

children: The Czech economy expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter, driven mainly by household consumption and investments, the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Friday.
Quarter-on-quarter growth confirmed flash estimate, year-on-year growth revised to 1.9% from 2.0%.
Final household consumption grew by 0.5% on the quarter and 2.7% year-on-year.
Government spending rose 0.1% and 1.0% on quarterly and year-on-year basis, respectively.
Investments measured by fixed capital formation rose by 1.5% quarterly and 7.1% year-on-year.
"The year-on-year rise was recorded mainly in investments in housing, other buildings and vehicles," the CSU said.

Of the 1.9% annual growth figure, household demand contributed 1.1 percentage points, government spending added 0.2 points, foreign trade also 0.2 points, and capital formation 1.7 points. A lower rise in inventories subtracted 1.3 points.
